claims.title: Sequential unauthenticated payment links disclose invoices to anyone who guesses an invoice number
claims.description: An internet attacker can request `flow:entity:payer>process:billing-app>open-payment-page` with a guessed invoice number. The flow has no authentication, while invoice numbers are sequential across companies; `process:billing-app` returns the invoice, company name, and payout bank details. This enables repeated enumeration of other tenants' payment information and supplies bank-detail and invoice data for targeted fraud.

quotes.text: Invoice numbers count up from 1000 across all companies.
The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details, and it asks the payer to sign in to nothing.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because the unauthenticated payment-page flow crosses from `boundary:internet` and invoice numbers are predictable. Impact is high because `process:billing-app` exposes financial invoice and payout-bank information plus PII across customer companies.

mitigations.summary: Require an unguessable, scoped payment capability
mitigations.detail: Replace invoice-number links with high-entropy, single-purpose payment tokens bound to one invoice and expiry, and reject direct invoice-number lookup from the payment page.
Show only the fields required to make the payment and avoid exposing payout-bank details or broader customer information before a valid capability is verified.

claims.title: A company user may conditionally retrieve another tenant's invoice by changing its sequential number
claims.description: A signed-in company user can ask `process:billing-app` to load an invoice by invoice number through `flow:entity:company-user>process:billing-app>manage-invoices`. The source leaves open whether the app verifies that the invoice belongs to that user's company, while invoice numbers are sequential across all companies. If that ownership check is absent, a user can elicit invoices, customer records, and payout-bank details belonging to other tenants; those details can then be used to target those tenants or exploit the payment workflow.

quotes.text: When a user opens an invoice, the billing app loads it by its invoice number. Nobody wrote down whether it also checks that the invoice belongs to the user's company. Invoice numbers count up from 1000 across all companies.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high conditional on the undocumented ownership check because any authenticated company user can submit invoice-number requests and the numbers are sequential. Impact is high because a successful cross-tenant response exposes financial, PII, and payout-bank data held by `process:billing-app`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce tenant ownership on every invoice read
mitigations.detail: Bind the requested invoice's company ID to the authenticated session server-side before loading or returning any invoice or related customer and payout data.
Do not expose sequential cross-tenant invoice numbers as lookup identifiers; use unguessable public references for user-facing routes.

claims.title: Any customer user can request PDFs containing another tenant's invoice data
claims.description: Any authenticated customer user can repeatedly ask `process:billing-app` for a PDF of any invoice. The app places the requested company ID and invoice number on `flow:process:billing-app>store:render-queue>queue-render-job`, and `process:pdf-renderer` trusts the company ID in that job when reading and rendering the invoice. A malicious tenant user can therefore elicit invoice PDFs for other companies, exposing financial and PII content and enabling bulk collection because requests are unrestricted.

quotes.text: It trusts the company ID the job carries. Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because the source explicitly says any user can request any invoice PDF repeatedly. Impact is high because the rendered PDFs contain other companies' financial invoices and PII, allowing corpus-scale cross-tenant disclosure.

mitigations.summary: Authorize PDF generation against the requesting tenant
mitigations.detail: At `process:billing-app`, verify that the requester may read the invoice before queuing a render job; do not accept a caller-controlled company ID as authorization.
Have `process:pdf-renderer` derive tenant context from a signed, short-lived job capability or independently re-check invoice ownership before reading the tenant database.
Limit PDF generation per tenant and alert on sequential or cross-tenant invoice request patterns.

claims.title: Tenant-database traffic may expose all companies' financial records if transport encryption is absent
claims.description: `flow:process:billing-app>store:tenant-database>read-and-write-tenant-data` carries invoices, customers, and payout bank details for every company, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the unverified transport protection is absent, an attacker able to observe the cloud-platform path can intercept the database traffic and read the multi-tenant corpus. The captured records enable targeted payment fraud and tenant-specific attacks without using the application read path.

quotes.text: The billing app connects with one database account for all companies.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown transport posture because the attacker needs an observation position on an intra-cloud-platform connection. Impact is high because the flow carries every company's financial, PII, and business-critical tenant data.

mitigations.detail: Configure TLS for `flow:process:billing-app>store:tenant-database>read-and-write-tenant-data`, validate the database identity, and use mTLS or equivalent workload authentication where supported.

claims.title: Render jobs may reveal tenant and invoice identifiers in transit
claims.description: `flow:process:billing-app>store:render-queue>queue-render-job` carries a company ID and invoice number, while both protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If that transport is plaintext, an observer on the cloud-platform path can intercept tenant-to-invoice mappings. Those identifiers can be used with the invoice-number-based application and payment-page paths to target specific records and companies.

quotes.text: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown internal transport protection because an attacker must observe the cloud-platform path. Impact is medium because the disclosed tenant and invoice identifiers map customers to financial records and facilitate later enumeration.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with authenticated queue endpoints for `flow:process:billing-app>store:render-queue>queue-render-job` and document the resulting protocol and transport-encryption state.

claims.title: Renderer retrieval of invoices may expose invoice content on an unverified internal channel
claims.description: `flow:process:pdf-renderer>store:tenant-database>read-invoice` reads invoice data, but its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport encryption is not present, an on-path cloud-platform attacker can intercept financial and PII invoice content while the renderer retrieves it. The data can be used for customer impersonation, payment fraud, and targeted disclosure beyond the renderer's intended job.

quotes.text: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time, reads the invoice from the tenant database

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown internal transport control because observation requires a cloud-platform path position. Impact is high because the renderer's database reads contain tenant invoice data tagged financial and PII.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate renderer database connections
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:pdf-renderer>store:tenant-database>read-invoice` to TLS with database identity validation and a renderer-specific credential.

claims.title: Invoice PDFs may be exposed while the renderer writes them to the bucket
claims.description: `flow:process:pdf-renderer>store:pdf-bucket>write-pdf` carries rendered invoice PDFs, but its protocol, authentication, and transport encryption are unknown. If the channel lacks encryption, an attacker observing the internal path can intercept invoice PDFs containing financial and PII data before storage. The copied PDFs can be retained and used outside the application's tenant controls.

quotes.text: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown internal channel protection because an attacker needs an on-path position. Impact is high because a rendered PDF preserves financial invoice data and PII in a portable form.

mitigations.detail: Use an authenticated TLS endpoint for `flow:process:pdf-renderer>store:pdf-bucket>write-pdf` and restrict the renderer credential to its required write prefix.

claims.title: PDF retrieval traffic may disclose invoice documents if internal transport is unencrypted
claims.description: `flow:process:billing-app>store:pdf-bucket>fetch-pdfs` fetches invoice PDFs for every company using one service credential, while its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If encryption is absent, an attacker on that cloud-platform path can intercept PDFs returned to `process:billing-app`, acquiring financial and PII documents without passing tenant-facing authorization checks. The documents can then support fraud against the affected companies.

quotes.text: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown internal transport control because interception requires access to the cloud-platform path. Impact is high because the flow retrieves invoice PDFs for all companies and those documents contain financial and PII content.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS and endpoint identity validation on `flow:process:billing-app>store:pdf-bucket>fetch-pdfs`; use a narrowly scoped workload identity rather than a broad shared service credential.

claims.title: Support-office observers may capture privileged admin-console credentials if the connection is unencrypted
claims.description: `flow:entity:support-agent>process:admin-console>use-admin-console` crosses from `boundary:support-office-network` to `boundary:cloud-platform` and carries an agent sign-in plus the customer user the agent will act as. Its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport protection is absent, an attacker on the support-office path can intercept an agent's credentials or authenticated session and use the admin-console capability to open sessions as customer users, reaching their billing information through `process:billing-app`.

quotes.text: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code. From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport control: the attacker needs a support-office network observation position, but the flow is a decided boundary crossing and carries reusable privileged session material. Impact is high because captured admin-console access enables sessions as any customer user and access to their financial and PII data.

mitigations.summary: Enforce TLS for the support-admin path
mitigations.detail: Require modern TLS with strict certificate validation for `flow:entity:support-agent>process:admin-console>use-admin-console`, and prevent insecure protocol fallback.

mitigations.summary: Bind privileged sessions to channel and device context
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, channel-bound sessions and require reauthentication before opening a session as a customer user.

claims.title: Customer-user session material may be exposed between the admin console and billing app
claims.description: `flow:process:admin-console>process:billing-app>open-session-as-customer-user` carries a session as a chosen customer user, but its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the internal connection is unencrypted, a cloud-platform on-path attacker can intercept that session material and read the selected customer's invoices, customer records, and payout information through `process:billing-app`. Because the admin console can select any customer user, repeated interception can broaden to multiple tenants.

quotes.text: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown internal transport protection because the attacker must observe the cloud-platform connection. Impact is high because the intercepted material represents customer-user sessions that can expose financial, PII, and business-critical tenant data.

mitigations.summary: Use mTLS for the impersonation-session call
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:admin-console>process:billing-app>open-session-as-customer-user` to mutually authenticated TLS and validate each workload identity.
Use an auditable, short-lived impersonation assertion bound to the support agent and target user rather than sending a reusable customer session.

claims.title: A storage copy may disclose the entire tenant database if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:tenant-database` contains every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that unresolved setting means storage is unencrypted, a person obtaining a decommissioned volume, snapshot, backup, or other operational copy can read the multi-tenant database directly without authenticating through `process:billing-app`. One copy would expose the corpus of financial and PII data and enable broad payment-fraud targeting.

quotes.text: Nobody recorded how the billing app and the renderer reach the database, the queue or the bucket, or how the database and the bucket are protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value because a storage copy bypasses the application but must first be obtained. Impact is high because `store:tenant-database` holds all companies' financial, PII, and business-critical records in one database.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce database encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual `encryption_at_rest` state of `store:tenant-database`, then require managed-key encryption for the primary database and every backup, snapshot, replica, and export.
Separate backup/export permissions from application access and limit key use to narrowly defined recovery and database workloads.

claims.title: A copied PDF bucket may expose every tenant's invoice documents if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:pdf-bucket` holds invoice PDFs for every company and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If encryption is not enabled, an attacker who obtains a bucket backup, export, or storage-layer copy can read the PDFs without using the billing app or satisfying tenant authorization. The portable documents disclose financial invoice information and PII for multiple customer companies.

quotes.text: Nobody recorded how the billing app and the renderer reach the database, the queue or the bucket, or how the database and the bucket are protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unresolved at-rest posture because an attacker must obtain an operational storage copy. Impact is high because `store:pdf-bucket` retains invoice PDFs containing financial and PII data for every company.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt PDF storage and all derived copies
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:pdf-bucket` encryption at rest and enforce managed-key encryption for the bucket, backups, exports, and replicas.
Use least-privilege bucket policies, separate export authority from application reads, and log anomalous bulk object access.

claims.title: Render-queue copies may disclose tenant-to-invoice mappings if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:render-queue` persists jobs containing a company ID and invoice number, but its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the queue's storage is unencrypted, a storage-copy attacker can read those jobs from an operational copy and map tenants to invoice identifiers. That metadata facilitates targeted invoice enumeration against the payment and billing-app paths, even though the queue does not itself hold full invoice content.

quotes.text: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest control because a copied queue store can be read without application access once obtained. Impact is medium because the disclosed company-ID and invoice-number mappings facilitate targeting of financial records rather than directly containing the full records.

mitigations.detail: Determine the at-rest protection for `store:render-queue` and require encryption for queue storage, backups, and any exported message data.
Use opaque job references rather than carrying directly usable company IDs and invoice numbers where the renderer can resolve the data through a protected lookup.
